result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.contracted_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Contract an edge by merging its endpoints. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15133-L15228){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.contracted_edge( u, v, self_loops=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Contract an edge](/assets/graphs/contracted-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph in two rows; B is outlined as the survivor and the edge B to E is contracted, so E and its three edges are in the accent color. After: E is gone, shown dashed; its edges to D and F now attach to B, and the contracted edge itself has become a self-loop on B, all in the accent color." width="100%"} Given an edge between `u` and `v`, creates a new graph where `v` is merged into `u`. This is equivalent to `contract_nodes(u, v)` but explicitly requires that an edge exists between the nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [u]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source endpoint of the edge (node ID or label). [v]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target endpoint of the edge (node ID or label). This node will be removed. [self_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), the contracted edge becomes a self-loop on `u`. If `False`, the contracted edge is removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with the edge contracted. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either node does not exist. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If no edge exists between `u` and `v`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Convenience wrapper around `contract_nodes(u, v)` that first checks an edge $(u, v)$ actually exists and raises `ValueError` if not. The distinction matters: `contract_nodes()` happily merges any two nodes, while `contracted_edge()` is the operation graph theorists usually mean when they talk about contracting *an edge*, so the guard rules out accidental merges of non-adjacent nodes. On undirected graphs edge orientation is irrelevant; on directed graphs either an $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ edge satisfies the precondition. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#f81f09e8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) result = g.contracted_edge("A", "B") result.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: "B"'s other connections carry over to "A", so the former `B-C` edge now appears as `A-C`: ::: {#8cbcabba .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.has_edge("A", "C") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: The same works on directed graphs -- contracting `A->B` redirects `B`'s outgoing edges to originate from `A` instead: ::: {#66de90fa .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) result = g.contracted_edge("A", "B") result.has_edge("A", "C") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
